The call is update({ orgId, supplierId: base._id, expectedVersion: base.revision, ...args, ...extra }). orgId is the typed organization id prop, supplierId is the typed id of the loaded record, expectedVersion is the edit revision of the record the form was loaded from, args is buildUpdate(base, values, reason) typed UpdateArgs (only changed fields; null clears, undefined leaves) and extra is memory.current.options typed SupplierCreateOptions from mergeConfirmations (the user's own answers). Every key is declared by the update validator with a compatible type. The later spread of extra is a ref-derived object the extractor cannot resolve, so it withdraws the values of every earlier key and reports taxJurisdiction as TYPE_UNKNOWN (value any, key declared). A local experiment that moved the unresolved spreads first made orgId, supplierId and expectedVersion provable, but the buildUpdate fields stay unknown because the extractor does not follow a function result, so no small rewrite removes this debt and it is accepted as unproven value debt. The backend authorizes the tenant and finance permission, compares expectedVersion with the edit token (SUPPLIER_VERSION_CONFLICT) and validates each field. The update validator is byte-identical in the deployed commit ed0c4e1b and in main, so the fingerprint should match the production spec; that match was not observed for this path (it is computed here against the locally rendered current spec). No runtime, concurrency or full-contract certification.
